title: His own style, influences and bebop
summary: Ferbos says he picks up bits from others rather than imitating, and will play bebop but is not a bebop player.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: What about your own style? You can play most any style? Oh no, I wouldn't say most any style, no.

But I mean we sort of imitate some styles. I mean but quite naturally each person has the only individual we are playing. But I mean who I would say is covered behind, I would know because I've listened at, when I used to listen to Bernie Berrigan play and you listen to maybe Harry James or you listen to these fallout formations, all the ones I mentioned to Barry about, well you get a little of each one in your playing and then you find that you, in fact, you know I don't play like you and you don't play like me.
You might hear me say I got that little part of what she did in there. I say oh that line myself, you know, except what he did in there. I say go down the line, even going for the rest of the day.
But I never really tried to imitate anybody really.

But if something they make you would like. And you were quite nice, you pick up on what somebody else makes. But I mean they said a copy like some of the other ones, copy completely behind Louis Armstrong. Or maybe just like you said Kidron Day or this day there, or Martin Bergman, or Harry James, some folks they patented completely behind them.

But I never did try to imitate really. But it's a dude that something, make something, I mean that's a certain part of playing a number, a little thing he'd make. And I like that. And I get that in my head, I get on my arm, I play that number, I put that in there, and that's what you mean, kind of like, something. I might hear myself, I hear me make it, and it's too easy to hear why I hear me playing it. And you like that? Well that's it easy, you know, I'm only playing seven numbers that's made. Can you play progressive? No.
Well what they call bebop, I mean I play bebop because I mean I've had it in music and played, but I mean just to only be a bebop player? No.
